main_text.p: ξόμαι. prꝫ.pass. ἐνδείγμαι. a.1.med. ἐνδεί-ξάμην ω αὶς demonstravi Heb.6.10. exhibui 2.Tim.4.14. a.1.med. imperat. ἔνδειξαι ἀδ-ω. 2.pl. ἐνδείξασϑε edite,ostendite. a.1.med.subj. ἐνδείξωμαι ἡ ἥτις.
᾽Ενδεκα οἱ εἰς τὸ, ἀκλιτὸν, undecim.ex ἓν ϑ δέκα.
᾽Ενδεκάτος ἡ ον undecimus a um, Apoc.21.20.
᾽Ενδέχομαι admitto,recipio.Fut.ἐνδέξομαι. P.ἐν-δέδεγμαι. ἐνδέχεται est impersonale & redditur fieri potest. οὐκ ἐνδέχεται fieri non potest, seu non contingit, Luc.13.33. τὸ ἐνδεχόμενον contingens.
᾽Ενδημέω ω incolo, apud populum meum maneo, 2.Cor.5.6. F.ἡσω. P.ἐνδεδήμηκα, ab ἔνδη-μος ὁ ἡ manens cum populo suo,qui nonit peregre. ex οὐ ϑ δήμος ὁ populus.

᾽Ενδιδύσκομαι induor,cum Accus.imperf. ἐνδι-δυσκόμην ἢ εἳ induebar,est frequentativum verbi ἐνδύομαι induor,quo luxus divitiis il-lius heluonis arguitur. Non tamen tam hoc quàm nominibus,quæ adduntur πορφύραν καὶ βύσσον,Luc.16.19.
᾽Ενδίκος ὁ ἡ justus a, ex οὐ ϑ δίκη ης ἡ jus. Vide paulo infrà,Rom.3.8.
᾽Ενδόμησις εως ἡ pila, prima longa. moles seu structura erecta ad mœnia fulcienda. ab in-ufitato
Note: the right-hand marginal notes (dense Greek and Latin references, partly cut off by the binding) are not transcribed here.

page.notes: The right margin column is heavily cut off and too faint for reliable transcription; its Greek and Latin references are omitted. Greek readings in the main text are approximate and may contain errors; the first paragraph's accentuation is uncertain.
